headline: Thanksgiving Day brings the storm to New York City: 1.5 to 2 inches of rain (locally up to 3), damaging wind gusts around 45 to 60 mph peaking in the afternoon and evening, and widespread moderate coastal flooding at both of Thursday's high tides.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Thanksgiving starts with low clouds and east-northeast winds building to about 25 to 30 mph with gusts of 35 to 40 mph during the morning, then rain turns moderate to heavy in the afternoon and winds climb to about 30 to 40 mph with gusts of roughly 45 to 60 mph (peaks possibly a bit higher), strongest in New York City and along the coast; the latest short-range model suggests the worst winds could come 2 to 3 hours later than forecast. A High Wind Warning runs from 10 AM Thursday to 1 AM Friday for New York City, Long Island and the Hudson, eastern Essex and eastern Union county areas of New Jersey, and a Wind Advisory from 10 AM Thursday to 5 AM Friday now covers the rest of the area north and west, including the rest of northeast New Jersey, Westchester, Rockland, Orange, Putnam and Connecticut. Moist air from the subtropics brings 1.5 to 2 inches of rain in general, with local amounts up to 3 inches, heavy downpours at times and an isolated thunderstorm possible. Late Thursday night a dry pocket ends the rain from southwest to northeast and winds turn southeast to south and ease to about 25 to 35 mph with gusts near 40 to 45 mph, though light rain or drizzle may linger.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Friday brings scattered showers as the strong storm center lingers nearby, with a breezy southwest wind gusting about 30 to 35 mph that turns west after midnight. Saturday looks dry with west winds gusting about 25 to 30 mph, easing Saturday night. The discussion gives no temperature details for these days.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Sunday stays dry and quiet, then showers are likely after midnight Sunday night as a front arrives. A chance of showers lingers Monday morning, with southwest gusts around 25 to 30 mph turning west in the afternoon and northwest Monday night. The discussion gives no detail beyond Monday.

coast: Gale- to storm-force east-northeast winds Thursday morning into Thursday night, on top of already-high tides after the recent full moon, make widespread moderate coastal flooding likely at both the Thursday morning and evening high tides, with potential for major flooding along the western Great South Bay and significant impacts around Peconic Bay and the Peconic River and along the western Long Island Sound shoreline; surge up the Hackensack, Hudson and Passaic rivers brings minor to moderate flooding. Thursday morning's tide is naturally higher by at least a foot, but the peak surge is expected Thursday afternoon and evening, so both tides may reach similar levels, and heavy rain during the evening tide could worsen coastal street flooding; forecasters leaned toward the higher-end water levels for a safety margin. Coastal Flood Warnings run 7 AM Thursday to 6 AM Friday for New York City, Long Island, northeast New Jersey's waterfront, southern Westchester and southwestern Connecticut, with an advisory for southern Middlesex and New London counties through 3 PM Friday. For Friday morning's high tide, Coastal Flood Advisories cover the north shore of Long Island, New York City (except southern Queens), northeast New Jersey, southern Westchester and southwestern Connecticut, where water should drain out and impacts be mainly minor, while a Coastal Flood Watch covers southern Queens, southern Nassau and southern Suffolk, where southwest winds could bring another round of moderate flooding, especially on the eastern Great South Bay. Ocean beaches see 8 to 12 foot breakers with widespread beach flooding, dune erosion and possible localized overwash; western Long Island Sound and the Twin Forks see 3 to 6 foot waves with dune erosion, splashover and possible isolated damage to shoreline and marina structures. On the water, a Gale Warning until 6 AM Thursday gives way to a Storm Warning from 6 AM Thursday to 1 AM Friday, with ocean seas over 20 feet late Thursday afternoon and evening and waves near 10 feet on the Sound and at the New York Harbor entrance; a southwest gale is likely on the ocean Friday, easing to small-craft-advisory levels Saturday and below that Sunday, with small-craft conditions possible again Monday, especially on the ocean.
watch_for: Thursday's strongest winds could arrive 1 to 3 hours later than forecast
Heavy downpours during Thursday evening's high tide worsening coastal street flooding
Friday morning's high tide on Long Island's south shore bays, under a Coastal Flood Watch
confidence: Models agree well on the Thanksgiving storm, with a few hours of uncertainty in the timing of peak winds, and the coastal flood forecast deliberately leans toward the higher end; the weekend and Monday get little detail.
